LiveDRM:
**If YTS CLI set up is not completed, please refer to "Testing with YTS CLI" section in READ ME tab for setting up YTS CLI.**

1) Run "yts discover". Numbers in parentheses are short IDs assigned to each device at discovery step.
2) Run yts launch {shortId} https://www.youtube.com/tv?list=OLAK5uy_mKAu6VNK3gMSq_L8fU_C6myQnuuuIzvWY
3) Double-check that the launched video has the LIVE badge, and enable "Stats for nerds".
4) Observe the video for about 18 minutes

Pass/Fail Criteria
- The "Live Latency" and "Live Mode" fields must appear in the Stats for nerds box.
- The "Protected" field in Stats for nerds must include "WVA", indicating the video is using Widevine DRM
- The "Dropped Frames" field in Stats for nerds should show no more than 0.5% of total frames were dropped
- There should be very few (ideally none at all) skipping, stuttering, buffering or pausing in video or audio.
- There should be no improperly decrypted video frames (typically seen as green and magenta artifacts)
12 Hour Endurance:
1) Run "yts discover". Numbers in parentheses are short IDs assigned to each device at discovery step.
2) Run yts test {short ID} --test-version=20250721  "In-app Video Endurance"

Pass/Fail Criteria
- This is an endurance test that must be played for 12 hours. If the device still runs after 12 hours, the test is a pass.
YouTube Music Endurance:
For this test you may need to enable screensaver if it is not already enabled. You can do this with the following command:

adb shell settings put secure screensaver_enabled 1

1) Make sure that the device screensaver and/or sleep mode are enabled.
2) Run "yts discover". Numbers in parentheses are short IDs assigned to each device at discovery step.
3) Run yts launch {short ID} https://www.youtube.com/tv#/watch?v=13EL6Mgeocc
4) Play the audio only playback till the screensaver activation time (plus a little bit more just to be sure).

Pass/Fail Criteria
- The screensaver must not activate and the device must not go to sleep mode.
Persistence Cookie 200 times:
1) Run "yts discover". Numbers in parentheses are short IDs assigned to each device at discovery step.
2) Run yts test {short ID} --test-version=20250721 "Persistence Cookie keeps cookie intact after 200 times of device on/off"

Note: If this test is interrupted in the middle, you can re-run it and it may pick up where it left off (unless the device crashed and/or cleared its storage).

Pass/Fail Criteria
- After the test runs, it will automatically return a "PASSED" or "FAILED" result visible on console and also the top right corner of the screen.
Live streaming:
1) Run "yts discover". Numbers in parentheses are short IDs assigned to each device at discovery step.
2) Run yts launch {short ID} "stick=0"
3) Run yts launch {short ID} "https://www.youtube.com/tv?c=UC4R8DWoMoI7CAwX8_LjQHig"
Above step will launch the YouTube app and deeplink to a special channel for ongoing livestreams. If it doesn't, then try the command again after 30 seconds. It should work after at most a couple of retries.
4) Play any video that has the "Live" badge rather than a duration.

Pass/Fail Criteria
- Playback should begin within a similar amount of time as static videos.
- Pause the video for 10 seconds and then resume - confirm this works normally.
- There should be little to no rebuffering/stuttering, and little to no bitrate changes during playback.
- Play the Live video for at least 10 minutes (note: A device should be capable of sustaining continuous playback of Live stream videos for at least 12 hours)
Adaptive Bit Rate:
1) Run "yts discover". Numbers in parentheses are short IDs assigned to each device at discovery step.
2) Run yts test {short ID} --test-version=20250721 --guided "Media Adaptive Bit Rate"
3) Follow the instruction on the screen

Pass/Fail Criteria
- Begin playing at a low resolution, and adapt to a higher resolution track.
- Smoothly transition to the new resolution
- No skipping, stuttering or pausing can occur in the video or audio
- Any issues with video or audio playback cause this test to fail

Note - This test can be marked as pass even if the playback resolution does not shift to the highest resolution supported by the DUT.

[Voice&Search] Soft-mic Button:
1) Launch the YouTube application
2) Navigate to the search page
3) A microphone icon should be visible next to the keyboard
4) Move focus to the microphone icon and press OK
5) Holding the microphone near your mouth and without pressing any buttons on the remote, say, "Eric Clapton solo".

Pass/Fail Criteria
- After Step #4, the screen must indicate that the device is now listening for audio input.
- After Step #5, the search page must show results for the query, "Eric Clapton solo", or begin direct playback.
Current Time:
1) Run "yts discover". Numbers in parentheses are short IDs assigned to each device at discovery step.
2) Run yts launch {short ID} "stick=0"
3) Run yts launch {short ID} "https://www.youtube.com/tv?env_showUIStats=true&use_toa=true&v=RgodTgI2EDo"
4) The above step will launch the YouTube app and deeplink to a special video that displays its current time over a background of colorful vertical bars. If it doesn't, then try the command again after 30 seconds. It should work after at most a couple of retries.
5) Observe the first 10 seconds of the video
6) Pause the video. When the video is paused, the currentTime value is updated and displayed in the top right corner.
7) Resume the video
8) Repeat steps 4-5 five times
9) Seek forward 40 seconds or more.
10) Repeat steps 4-5 five times
11) Seek backwards 40 seconds or more
12) Repeat steps 4-5 five times.

Pass/Fail Criteria
- At all times during the test, the time displayed in the overlay must be within 100 milliseconds of the time displayed in the paused video.

In-app HDR HLG:
If the device does not intend to support HDR, you may skip this test. Otherwise the instructions are as follows:

1) Run "yts discover". Numbers in parentheses are short IDs assigned to each device at discovery step.
2) Run yts launch {shortId} https://www.youtube.com/tv?v=5w58p6iVhPc
3) Enable "Stats for nerds" without pausing video playback.

Pass/Fail Criteria
- In "Stats for nerds", the "Codecs" field must indicate HDR playback (the value must include "vp09.02", or "av01.0.##M.10" where # is any numeric digit)
- In "Stats for nerds", the "Color" field must indicate that the eotf is arib-std-b67 (HLG) and colorspace is bt2020
- The display (whether native or plugged in) must automatically switch to "HDR mode". This is sometimes indicated by a pop-up at a corner of the screen, but the exact behavior is device-dependent.

In-app Visual Audio / Video Sync:
1) Run "yts discover". Numbers in parentheses are short IDs assigned to each device at discovery step.
2) Run yts launch {shortId} "https://www.youtube.com/tv?list=PLT2JIu9jdshqNyrN5gzxaihngAjwFOFMB"
3) Enable "Stats for nerds" and verify that the "Current" frame rate is the same as the "Optimal" frame rate (typically 60 but can also be 30) at all times.
4) For each video in the playlist:
- Play the video for about 30 seconds
- Pause the video, and then resume a few seconds later.
- Seek forward by at least 10-15 seconds. Let it play from this new position for a few seconds.
- Seek backward by at least 10-15 seconds. Let it play from this new position for a few seconds.

Pass/Fail Criteria
- In Stats for nerds, the "Current" and "Optimal" frame rates should roughly match (typically both are ~60 but other numbers are allowed too so long as they match)
- Audio and video must stay in sync (as perceived by the tester) through all of the steps above.
DRM Purchased Movie:
This test requires a YouTube account to purchase a test asset (at $0.00 cost). Refer to the README tab for links to public facing articles on how to purchase movies inside the YouTube app.

1) Run "yts discover". Numbers in parentheses are short IDs assigned to each device at discovery step.
2) Run yts launch {shortId} https://www.youtube.com/tv?v=MeFoUwes8nE

Note: The above command will launch the YouTube app with a link to a purchasable movie. If the movie is not available in your region, run yts launch {shortID} https://www.youtube.com/tv?v=iNvUS1dnwfw instead for an alternate asset. In the notes column to the right, mention that you used the alternate asset.

3) Purchase the target movie (at $0.00 cost).
4) Play the video and enable "Stats for Nerds". Let the video play for about 60 seconds.

Pass/Fail Criteria
- In "Stats for nerds", there should be a "key system" and/or "protected" field whose value must include "WVA", indicating the video is using Widevine DRM.
- In "Stats for nerds", the "Optimal Resolution" MUST equal the actual maximum resolution supported by the device.
Multi-App Performance:
This test occasionally throws an error with a cryptic error code. If this happens, please wait a few minutes and then retry the test. If and only if the test throws the exact same error code 3 times in a row, you may mark the test as N/A. Please do not mark N/A if the test runs without errors, even if the overall result is a failure.

1) Run "yts discover". Numbers in parentheses are short IDs assigned to each device at discovery step.
2) Run yts launch {shortId} https://www.youtube.com/tv?automationRoutine=certPerformanceRoutine&samples=100&use_toa=true&hl=en-US&gl=en_US
3) The above command will launch an automated performance routine. Wait for it to complete and record the stats displayed at the end.
4) Exit the YouTube app and launch another OTT media app.
5) Browse through the new app and initiate playback of at least 5 different videos.
6) Relaunch YouTube again with the command from Step 2.
7) Once again wait for the automated routine to complete and record its stats.

Pass/Fail Criteria
- In both Step 3 and Step 7, the final stats displayed on screen must be as follows:
  - Pct50 value for "Browse to watch" <= 1500ms
  - Pct95 value for "Row to Row" >= 30
  - Pct95 value for "Tile to Tile" >= 30
  - Pct95 value for "Input Latency" < 200ms
- If a single stat is outside of the allowed range in either run of the automation routine, the test is a FAIL. Otherwise it is a PASS.
System Overlay:
This test occasionally throws an error with a cryptic error code. If this happens, please wait a few minutes and then retry the test. If and only if the test throws the exact same error code 3 times in a row, you may mark the test as N/A. Please do not mark N/A if the test runs without errors, even if the overall result is a failure.

If the device does not support any system overlays (e.g. system menu, picture or sound settings, mute icon, etc.) then you may mark this test as N/A. Otherwise please follow these instructions:

1) Run "yts discover". Numbers in parentheses are short IDs assigned to each device at discovery step.
2) Run yts launch {shortId} https://www.youtube.com/tv?automationRoutine=certPerformanceRoutine&samples=16&use_toa=true&hl=en-US&gl=en_US
3) The above command will launch an automated performance routine. Wait for it to complete and record the stats displayed at the end.
4) Exit the YouTube app.
5) Re-launch the automation routine with the same command as Step 2 but this time, within the first 1-2 minutes of the routine, open a system overlay (settings menu, mute icon, etc).
6) Wait for the routine to finish and record the stats at the end.

Pass/Fail Criteria
- If Step 5 caused a visually apparent degradation of performance (slowed transitions, stuttering, excessive video buffering), the test is a FAIL.
- In both Step 2 and Step 6, the final stats displayed on screen must be as follows:
  - Pct50 value for "Browse to watch" <= 1500ms
  - Pct95 value for "Row to Row" >= 30
  - Pct95 value for "Tile to Tile" >= 30
  - Pct95 value for "Input Latency" < 200ms
- If a single stat is outside of the allowed range in either run of the automation routine, the test is a FAIL. Otherwise it is a PASS.
Sign-in Persistence:
1) Run "yts discover". Numbers in parentheses are short IDs assigned to each device at discovery step.
2) Run `yts launch {shortId}` to launch the YouTube app.
3) Sign in to a YouTube account (from the account icon on the top left)
4) Exit YouTube.
5) Fully unplug the device from power, wait 90 seconds, and plug it back in.
6) Run `yts launch {shortId}` to launch the YouTube app again.

Pass/Fail Criteria
- If YouTube is still signed in to the same account that you signed in with for this test, mark the test as PASSED. Otherwise the test is FAILED.
